invariants: Optional control_item_at_point appends at offset 576, preserving all previous methods. API version stays 1 with size 584. Separate acceptance and uint64 output distinguish unsupported queries from native non-item areas without losing ID bits.

GNUstep owns the original hitTest, native coordinate conversion and NSMatrix getRow:column:forPoint: lookup. The provider maps the resulting original cell to existing application row IDs. No view/control subclass or row, clipping, scrollbar, drawing or hit algorithm is copied.

The shared host view-hit helper also serves existing native wheel dispatch. Item queries do not alter selection, focus or actions, and remain readable during native tracking. Invalid controls/coordinates/output are rejected without changing caller output.

Owned operation 53 uses the unchanged generic request with x/y and returns exactly one uint64 ID, zero for native non-item areas. Bootstrap part 2.x advertises support independently of unchanged list and scroll capability fields. ItemHits.inc is one reusable engine/toolkit transport helper.

Independent ordinary NSBrowser windows supply a grid of more than 700 native hit observations per state at actual 1x/2x, covering clip edges, scrollers, off-control points, scroll positions, empty lists and disabled controls/cells. Shared C transport preserves IDs above the exact-double range and rejects other connections.

Actual previous API 1/576 and 1/568 providers remain usable, reject missing optional methods without caller writes, and preserve existing list/scroll behavior. An unchanged compiled previous list client passes against the new SDK.

Only the isolated shared SDK and probes are built. Existing browser adapters are unchanged and retain original toolbar/address bar/tabs. All 20 measured production hashes and package inventory remain unchanged. Browser content processes retain Seccomp=2 and NoNewPrivs=1.

This checkpoint exposes the native hit decision; it does not replace the original browser event target yet. The known Chromium DOM mousedown row mismatch remains open and is not claimed fixed. Subsequent browser/toolkit adapters must map native IDs through their original hit-result lifetime and trusted event/cancellation paths.
